recipes.name: Grandma's Baked Rice Pudding with Meringue

steps.text: Bring water and rice to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to low, stir, and cover pan. Simmer until water is absorbed, about 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat ½ cup sugar and egg yolks together in a bowl. Beat in cornstarch and salt; continue beating. Gradually beat in milk. Stir in cooked rice, raisins, and lemon juice; transfer to a baking dish and place inside a larger baking pan. Fill larger pan with water 1 inch up the sides of the smaller baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until pudding is creamy and most liquid is absorbed, stirring occasionally, about 1 hour, 30 minutes. Add more water to the larger baking pan as necessary to maintain the level.

Meanwhile, beat egg whites in a glass or ceramic bowl until soft peaks form. Gradually beat in ¼ cup sugar; continue beating until meringue forms stiff peaks. Remove pudding from the oven, leaving it in the larger baking pan. Top pudding with meringue, swirling with a spoon to create soft peaks.
Increase the oven temperature to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until meringue is golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Serve warm.

review.reviewBody: This is terrific! I've been trying a lot of the rice pudding recipes and find this one to be one of my favorites so far. I had some left over rice and used that but otherwise followed the recipe. It was easy and the pudding firmed up nicely even though I thought that it was a little to liquidy at first. Thanks

Wonderfully unctuous, creamy and super tasty treat. I added cinnamon and a touch of nutmeg and cloves. I also soaked the raisins in dark rum for two weeks. This is reminiscent of mother’s rice pudding. Love it.

Thanks for this recipe—the meringue adds a fun twist to the basic baked custard recipe. I'm not a big fan of baked pudding because it's never as smooth as desktop or slow-cooker pudding, but this adds a fun way to use the leftover egg whites as meringue that looks so appealing! 

Here's my variation: I made slow-cooker rice pudding then added meringue at the end; here's how: Prepare your favorite slow cooker recipe as described, but refrigerate the egg whites while the rice pudding cooks. During the last 1/2 hour of cooking, follow the meringue preparation for this recipe and remember to preheat the oven. Transfer the pudding to a large baking dish and spoon the meringue mixture on top, making peaks with the spoon. Bake until meringue is cooked and golden approx. 8-10 minutes.

This was a bit more work than most Rice Puddings I have made. But I think it was worth it. It was a bit dry after it was completely done, I mixed the topping in well with the pudding and then added some evaporated milk to bring it back to the creamier stage, it was fabulous!!!

I've been making rice pudding this way for years - I sometimes omit the raisins and put a thin layer of raspberry jam on top of the pudding before putting on the meringue - it really is quite good too.

I wasn't very impressed with this recipe. The preparation is complicated and the results weren't good enough to justify the effort. There are easier ways to make a better, smoother rice pudding. Also, with the added meringue the dish was too sweet. If you plan to make it I suggest reducing the amount of sugar in the meringue by about half. In its favor, the finished dish looks wonderful.
Very good! Takes time, but it's worth the effort!
My Husband concurs it was delicious
i liked it it was very good and i did it with little to no experience

My wife grew up eating rice pudding...this is now her favorite! will make it as one of the deserts for Thanksgiving.
Easy and she loves it when I make it for her.
Yes I will make it again. Upon tasting it the pudding needed longer cooking time but the liquid was running low.
delicious! the only rice pudding i will eat and it is my son's favorite. i did not do the meringue or raisons. i did add a generous dash of cinnamon. very good.

This is a great recipe...but...I don't get the meringue. I feel like such a traitor! I am a meringue enthusiast, I am! BUT in this recipe it just seemed so out of place. I felt like I was having two separate desserts together and missing the lemon filling or something. Next time I'll skip the meringue or maybe just make a pie if I'm in such a mood.
